Preserved the accepted SAS source filters, winsorization, predictor/outcome construction, full-rank annual OLS screen, Stata xtfmb estimator, horizon-specific fits, and Newey–West lag 3. Kept fit_year through the handoff and instrumented each fit to print original-period and added-period counts from the active e(sample), plus its last contributing fit_year.
Used only the six local COMP/CRSP SAS sources named in the accepted construction; no external or substitute data were introduced.

limitations: The paper does not specify the rolling-window endpoint convention, dividend mnemonic, primary-link selection rule, or Newey-West lag; the best-effort choices are documented in design.md.
Source support starts at 1963, shorter than a literal ten-year window for the earliest origin years; early origins use available historical rows and never post-origin outcomes.
Provider currency tables begin in the local 1980s vintage; non-USD monetary fields without exact, unique, positive dated rates remain missing while USD observations remain eligible.
The installed xtfmb lag option supplies individual coefficient HAC standard errors but zeroes off-diagonal covariances, so joint HAC inference is not reported.

The resource-catalog path recorded in the assigned work item was not present; exact source paths and fields came from the assigned feasibility record and each named source was checked directly. The SAS files do not embed vendor release labels, so current local identifies the on-disk versions used, not a separately verified vendor release date.
